archetype.name: Pocket Passer (rhythm-and-timing)
archetype.definition: A 38-year-old who wins from the pocket by getting the ball out on time, avoiding sacks and attacking the 10-to-20-yard window, with essentially no running game beyond sneaks.

report.headline: Productive veteran arm, but his numbers came elsewhere and Minnesota's cupboard is bare
report.take:
Cousins has been what he has nearly always been: an on-schedule pocket passer whose value lives past the sticks. His 0.15 EPA per dropback ranks 13th of 54 and sits far above the league's -0.021. His 22 touchdowns rank 2nd, and the 3.9% sack rate ranks 5th. The jump from last year is real in the charting, not just the box score. CPOE is up 4.1 points, yards per attempt up 0.96, and his bad-throw rate is down a point. He is also more aggressive than in his prime, throwing into tight windows 19.65% of the time, against career marks mostly in the low-to-mid teens.

The engine is downfield. Throws of 10+ air yards produced 0.47 EPA per attempt and 56.9 EPA in total, while everything under 10 yards added 0.7 combined. That short game is dragged down by screens and swing passes behind the line, which cost 18.4 EPA. Third down is where he earns his keep: 0.368 EPA a play, 11 touchdowns against one interception, and a 48.5% conversion rate needing 7.1 yards on average.

What the season line hides is context. His target list is Brock Bowers, Ashton Jeanty, Tre Tucker and Michael Mayer, and Bowers alone accounts for 31.6 EPA. None of those names appear on Minnesota's books. The Vikings' QB starts list Kyler Murray and Carson Wentz through Week 9, with Cousins's first start coming in Week 10 at Green Bay. So the 54 EPA and the top-10 fantasy finish were built in a different offense. His Minnesota sample is one conservative game: 207 yards, 2 TDs, a 2.56-second release and just 5.6 intended air yards.

The new situation is harsher. This offense ranks 30th in EPA and 28th passing. Jordan Addison (92% of snaps) is out after thumb surgery, Jauan Jennings is out, and T.J. Hockenson is out but trending toward a return. Murray, the incumbent, has a projected return date of November 29. Cousins is a capable starter holding a job that may be short-term, throwing to a depleted room behind the league's best defense. That defense should keep games close, but it won't spread the ball around for him.

strengths.title: Wins in the intermediate and deep zones
strengths.body: His 10+ air-yard throws carry the whole passing game, and the deep ball has been especially efficient with a +7.2 CPOE on 33 attempts. That 33-attempt deep sample will cool, but intermediate timing throws have been his career calling card. The bigger question is whether Minnesota's healthy receivers can run those routes, not whether he can still make the throws.

strengths.title: Sack avoidance under pressure
strengths.body: He converts pressure into sacks less often than any qualifier, 14.1% against a field where that rate routinely runs past 20%. His career pressure-to-sack marks were good but not this good, so some of this is a quick-processing year plus some luck. Still, a 3.9% sack rate is a skill floor he carries into any offense.

strengths.title: Third-down conversion engine
strengths.body: On third down he's been at his best: 0.368 EPA a play with 11 TDs and one interception. That reflects his comfort throwing past the sticks in obvious passing downs, and it is consistent with his history as a high-success-rate passer.

concerns.title: New team, gutted receiving room
concerns.body: His production was built with Bowers as the focal point, and Minnesota is now without Addison and Jennings, with Hockenson's status uncertain. Week 10 showed the adjustment: a 5.6-yard intended air distance, nearly three yards below his season norm. That is a game plan protecting a new quarterback, not his natural profile, and it caps his ceiling until bodies return.

concerns.title: Interceptions in the aggressive window
concerns.body: Nine picks rank 49th of 54. Five came on intermediate throws, the same zone that drives his value. Over the last three games his interception rate is 4.5%, 1.9 points above his season mark, including a three-pick game against San Francisco. This is the price of the higher aggressiveness, and with weaker receivers contesting catches it could get worse before it gets better.

concerns.title: Red-zone TDs outrun the efficiency
concerns.body: Sixteen red-zone touchdowns came with only a 34.9% success rate there. That is a touchdown haul out of line with how efficient those snaps were. Paired with a 6.4% TD rate above most of his career seasons, the scoring pace is the likeliest thing to regress, especially in a 30th-ranked offense.

trend.note: The five-game rates sit almost exactly on his season, but the weekly swings are wide: -5.2 EPA against the Rams, +14.2 against the Jets, then three interceptions in San Francisco. The last three games show sharper accuracy, with a 7.1 CPOE, alongside more turnovers.

nextGame.headline: Clean pocket likely, but thin targets meet a stingy deep defense
nextGame.body:
San Francisco's pass defense is middling overall (17th in EPA), and it barely gets home, ranking 31st in sack rate. That suits a pocket passer who already avoids sacks. The problem is where it gives ground. The 49ers are 4th against deep passes and 6th at limiting explosive completions, yet 24th against short throws, and backs draw an outsized share of targets against them. That pushes Cousins toward the underneath game that has been his weakest area all year. With SF's offense ranked 1st in EPA and Minnesota a 3-point road underdog, volume could rise late if the Vikings trail.

Availability tilts against him. Addison and Jennings are out, and Hockenson is reported as progressing but not cleared, so his likely top options are a patched-together group. On the other side, starting corner Renardo Green (93% of snaps) is questionable with a back injury, Nate Hobbs remains on IR, and two rotational defensive tackles are on IR. A Green absence would open the outside, which matters most if Cousins is allowed to push the ball. He threw three interceptions in his Week 9 visit there.

keyMatchups.title: Light rush versus a quick release
keyMatchups.body: SF's 4.5% sack rate and thinned interior give Cousins time he rarely wastes, given his league-best pressure-to-sack rate. A clean pocket keeps him on schedule and limits drive-killing negatives.

keyMatchups.title: Deep shots into a top-4 deep defense
keyMatchups.body: His best throws travel 20+ yards, and that is where SF is stingiest. Expect the plan to live underneath, where SF is soft but where he has added little EPA all season.

keyMatchups.title: Green's back and the outside corners
keyMatchups.body: With Hobbs on IR, a Green absence leaves SF thin at corner. That would give Minnesota's depleted receivers a fair chance on the perimeter.

nextGame.watch: Whether Hockenson is active. A real tight-end target is the closest thing Minnesota has to the Bowers role that drove his season.

restOfSeason.body:
The skill set holds: sack avoidance, third-down timing and intermediate accuracy have shown up across a decade. What won't carry over cleanly is the volume and scoring built in a better passing environment. Minnesota's offense is 30th in EPA, its top receivers are hurt, and the league's best defense should keep game scripts close. That means fewer forced shootouts. Expect something nearer 210-250 yards a game with touchdowns in the 1.3-1.9 range, as the red-zone TD rate cools. Interceptions should stay near a pick a game while he keeps throwing into tight windows with lesser targets.

The larger unknown is the job itself. Murray carries a November 29 projected return. If he's healthy, Cousins's run as the starter could be a few weeks, not the rest of the season. If Murray lingers and Addison and Hockenson return, Cousins has the profile to post a respectable 16-18 PPR points a game, not the 18.8 he managed elsewhere.
swingFactors: Kyler Murray's hamstring and return date
How far O'Connell lets him push the ball downfield

confidence.note: One game with Minnesota; season stats built with a different supporting cast; starting job may be temporary.
